As our Business Development Representative for EMEA, you are the first voice of Elliptic. You will open conversations with crypto businesses, financial institutions and public sector organisations, and book the meetings that turn into pipeline for our Account Executives and growth for the company.

By month 3, you will be booking 12 qualified meetings a month, with a clear route from here into our Inside Sales seat.

What you'll bring

  • Outbound prospecting experience, for example as an SDR, BDR or in a similar sales role, with a track record of hitting meeting or pipeline targets

  • Clear, credible communication with senior people, in writing and on the phone, in excellent English plus an additional European language and/or experience selling to UK and European prospects

  • Discipline with process, CRM data (HubSpot or Salesforce) and follow-up

  • Fluency with AI tools as part of your daily workflow, you use them to move faster and think better, and you know when not to trust them

What you'll do

  • Map the buying group on priority accounts and get past your first contact to the person who decides

  • Use AI every day to research accounts, personalise outreach at volume and prepare meeting briefs, and share what is landing with Sales, Marketing and Product

What we offer you

  • Hybrid working, with a real budget for your home office and up to 90 days a year fully remote

  • Generous leave, including a sabbatical and enhanced parental leave regardless of gender or path to parenthood

  • An annual learning and development budget, plus access to some of the most interesting minds in the industry

  • Comprehensive healthcare and full access to mental health support

  • A team that takes raising the bar seriously

We hire for trajectory as much as track record. If this sounds like you, apply even if you don't tick every box, we'd genuinely rather meet you than miss you.
descriptions.job-0wvqbct:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About TRM

TRM Labs is on a mission to build a safer world by fighting crime and protecting the people who investigate it. We started as a blockchain intelligence company, helping law enforcement, government agencies, financial institutions, and businesses detect, investigate, and disrupt crypto-enabled crime. Today our platform reaches well beyond the blockchain: we fuse on-chain data with cyber and open-source intelligence (OSINT) so investigators can move from a single crypto address to the full story behind a criminal network. Our blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms turn fragmented signals into fast, defensible investigative leads for the teams protecting public safety and national security every day.

TRM Academy delivers training and certification for the global community of investigators, analysts, and compliance professionals who detect and prevent fraud and financial crime involving cryptocurrencies. Learners get live and virtual courses, practical exercises, and a community of the world's experts in blockchain, crypto compliance, and financial crime investigations.

About the Role

As the Lead Instructor, EMEA, you will own the design and delivery of TRM Academy training across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, with blockchain intelligence and crypto investigations at the core of what you teach. You will turn complex on-chain concepts into practical, mission-ready skills for law enforcement, national security, and government audiences, and you will be equally comfortable teaching crypto businesses, exchanges, and financial institutions. Cyber and OSINT tradecraft is the complement: you will show investigators how to pair it with on-chain tracing to build a complete case.

EMEA is a region where we win by showing up. You will deliver in person, in the room, with customers across the UK, DACH, the Nordics and Baltics, France, and beyond, and you will work closely with our regional sales, value engineering, and customer success teams so that training drives adoption and opens the next conversation. You will join a Training Team of master instructors who can command a room, build engaging content, and speak to every level of expertise. We know how our products are used in the real world and help our customers become humble masters too.

This is also a build role. EMEA training is a growing opportunity, and you will help shape how it is scoped, packaged, and delivered as the region scales.

Please note: this role requires travel of 50-75%, primarily across EMEA.

The Impact You'll Have Here

  • Program manage and deliver live, in-person, and virtual blockchain intelligence training to law enforcement, national security, and government learners across EMEA.

  • Teach crypto fundamentals through advanced investigations on TRM's blockchain intelligence and AI intelligence platforms, helping investigators trace funds and build complete, defensible cases.

  • Develop and maintain curriculum, labs, and practical exercises that stay current with the crypto threat landscape, including fraud, scams, ransomware, hacks and exploits, terrorism finance, sanctions evasion, and money laundering typologies.

  • Adapt content for regional legal frameworks, case types, and audience maturity, from first-time crypto investigators to experienced national security analysts.

  • Pair on-chain tracing with cyber and OSINT techniques in courses and case walkthroughs, so learners can pivot from off-chain signals to blockchain activity.

  • Partner with sales, value engineering, and customer success to scope training engagements, support onboarding and enablement, and turn training into adoption and expansion.

  • Build relationships with law enforcement and industry partners across the region to grow the TRM Academy cadre and learner community.

  • Develop train-the-trainer materials and instructor guides so the Academy can scale in EMEA and coach other instructors as the team grows.

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5+ years of experience instructing courses, leading trainings, or delivering technical instruction.

  • Blockchain, cryptocurrency, or digital assets subject matter expertise (core requirement), ideally from hands-on on-chain investigations or crypto-enabled crime casework.

  • Law enforcement or government experience, or a proven track record training these audiences. Police and financial crime investigators are especially welcome.

  • Eligibility to obtain a government security clearance in the UK or another EMEA country.

  • Fluent English, written and spoken.

  • Experience building coursework, curriculum, labs, and appropriate testing.

  • Comfortable training private-sector audiences, such as crypto businesses/VASPs, exchanges, and financial institutions.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills and the ability to command the room.

  • Willingness and ability to travel 50-75% across EMEA.

  • AI fluency (part of our performance review process and of the interview process).

Nice to Have

  • Professional fluency in German (strongly preferred, given the size of our DACH opportunity).

  • Fluency in French, or in a Nordic, Baltic, or Eastern European language.

  • An existing national security clearance.

  • Experience in or alongside a national security, intelligence, or financial intelligence unit.

  • Working knowledge of cyber investigations, OSINT, and/or cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tradecraft.

  • Relevant certifications (for example GIAC credentials such as GCTI or GOSI, or similar cyber and OSINT credentials).

  • A Nordic, Baltic, or Eastern European background in crypto, particularly with national security experience.

A Note on AI Fluency

TRM is an AI-native company. We expect our instructors to already be using AI tools in their day-to-day work to accelerate research, author and refine training content, and speed up investigative and analytical workflows. AI fluency is not awareness or interest; it is production usage. It is evaluated in our interview process and is part of our performance review process.

Why This Role Matters

Investigators and analysts across Europe are facing crypto-enabled crime at growing scale, from fraud and ransomware to sanctions evasion and terrorism finance. By teaching them to trace funds on TRM's platforms and combine that with cyber and OSINT tradecraft, you directly increase how quickly and confidently they can detect, investigate, and disrupt the threats that put people at risk. Every cohort you train turns abstract concepts into concrete skills they can apply to active cases that week, and you will help define how TRM Academy shows up across EMEA.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe's Money Management products (Financial Accounts, Treasury, Global Payouts, Issuing, and Capital) let businesses and platforms hold, move, spend, and earn on their money using the same infrastructure they already use for payments. APAC Money as a Service (MaaS) is a newly formed team, based in Singapore, responsible for bringing this product suite to Asia-Pacific markets, enabling global businesses and platforms to use these capabilities directly or offer them to their APAC users, and building the local rails, compliance, and partner integrations that make it all work.

None of this works without financial partners: the banks, card networks, and licensed institutions whose systems our products run on in each market. Technical Operations in APAC MaaS owns the day-to-day health of those partner integrations, existing and new, and the working technical relationship with the partners behind them. We sit between product and platform engineering, Stripe's partnerships and compliance teams, and our partners' technical teams, which gives us an unusually complete view of how money moves in the region: the code and the real-world mechanics behind it.

What you'll do

This role sits where Stripe's engineering meets the financial institutions we build on, and it is broader than most technical operations seats. You'll own the health of the partner integrations that power APAC MaaS, and you'll be the technical face of Stripe to the banks, networks, and institutions behind them. One week that means working through a partner specification and reconciling settlement files; the next, shipping tooling or running an operational review with a partner's engineering team. Because every APAC launch depends on partner readiness, you'll have direct line of sight into what the team ships and a real say in how. It's a role that builds technical depth and partner judgment at the same time, in a region where we're still writing the playbook.

Responsibilities

  • Own the operational health of APAC MaaS's financial partner integrations across accounts, payouts, and card issuing: monitor them, catch problems early, and drive issues to root cause and durable fixes.
  • Act as the primary technical point of contact for our partners in the region. Run recurring operational reviews, manage escalations end to end, align on product usage and specifications, and keep both Stripe and the partner on track against their commitments.
  • Lead partner-facing technical change: onboarding and certifying new integrations, specification changes, migrations and cutovers, and incident reviews, coordinating Stripe engineering, partnerships, compliance, and the partner's teams.
  • Investigate and resolve issues across the stack. Read and write code, query data, work through logs and partner reports and files, and make scoped changes in Stripe's codebase when that is the right fix.
  • Build reconciliation and anomaly detection so that money moving through our partner integrations is correct, traceable, and accounted for, in collaboration with engineering, accounting, and partnerships.
  • Remove manual work through code, tooling, or changes to how we operate with partners.
  • Become the team's domain expert on how money actually moves in each APAC market: rails, cutoffs, settlement cycles, file formats, return codes, and partner-specific behavior. Document it and make it usable by the rest of the team.
  • Bring partner realities into product and engineering decisions, and define what "partner-ready" means for each market launch.

Who you are

You're equally at home in a partner's steering call and in a debugger, and you enjoy moving between the two. You are precise: you read the specification to the end, you notice when a reconciliation is off by one record, and you follow up until the loose end is closed. You build trust with external counterparts by being prepared, direct, and reliable, and you can hold a partner (or Stripe) to a commitment while keeping the relationship strong.

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 6+ years in a technical role (for example Technical Operations, Software Engineering, Integration Engineering, or Solutions Architecture), including meaningful time working directly with external technical counterparts
  • Experience owning working relationships with external partners such as banks, card networks, processors, or similar institutions: running operational reviews, managing escalations, and driving technical changes to completion across organizations
  • Ability to write high-quality, maintainable code and SQL, read and navigate an unfamiliar codebase, and make scoped changes safely; familiarity with developer tools such as Git
  • Knowledge of payments or money movement technologies and ecosystems, such as bank transfers, payouts, card issuing, settlement, or reconciliation
  • Exceptional attention to detail, with a track record of working from specifications, file formats, and financial data where small errors have real consequences
  • Great communication skills, both oral and written, with the ability to frame messages for technical and non-technical audiences inside and outside Stripe
  • Great problem-solving skills, with an ability to develop a working understanding of a technical system using a variety of methods: reading and writing code, writing SQL queries, reading documentation or partner specifications, running debugging programs, reading logs, asking well-formed questions of domain experts, or digging into the raw data

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with banking and payment rails, settlement, and reporting conventions in Asia-Pacific markets such as Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, or New Zealand
  • Experience taking a new partner integration live: certification, go-live, and hypercare
  • Experience with card issuing, processor, or network integrations, or with ledgering and financial data quality
  • Experience working with distributed teams and partners across US, European, and APAC time zones
  • Experience using AI tools to improve execution, quality, and effectiveness

Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner.

The opportunity

  • Program Integration

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

 

As a Blockchain Engineer at HIFI you will help own on-chain systems day to day. You'll build and maintain the integrations, smart contracts, and wallet infrastructure that connect HIFI's payments products to the chains and stablecoins we support. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll design how funds move and settle on-chain, work with the rest of engineering to connect those flows to our ledger and APIs, and partner with compliance on controls like wallet screening and transaction monitoring. You'll also be the person the team relies on to judge when a new chain or protocol is ready for production use.

 

What you will build

  • Wallet infrastructure, including key management, transaction signing, and orchestration across custodial and programmatic wallets.

  • Onchain transaction handling across EVM chains and the other networks we support, including gas, nonce management, and retries.

  • Stablecoin minting, burning, and settlement logic that connects USDC and other stablecoins to fiat rails for our on-ramp and off-ramp products.

  • Integrations with centralized and decentralized exchanges for swaps and liquidity routing, and cross-chain bridging between networks.

  • A double-entry ledger that keeps onchain balances, banking partners, and customer accounts in sync, with automated reconciliation.

  • Event listeners, confirmation tracking, and webhooks that give our platform and customers real-time visibility into onchain activity.

  • Idempotent transaction pipelines with failure recovery and screening hooks, so money moves correctly even when something goes wrong.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 3+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1 to 2 years building blockchain systems in production.

  • Deep familiarity with EVM chains, including transaction lifecycles, gas mechanics, common failure modes, and enough Solidity to read and integrate contracts.

  • Experience with wallet architecture, such as custody models, signing services, or MPC and HSM-backed setups.

  • Strong backend fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, and handling consistency and concurrency in distributed systems.

  • You build financial systems with reconciliation and audit trails by default.

  • You communicate clearly in code review and in writing.

 

Nice to have

  • Experience with stablecoin infrastructure such as Circle, or with connecting onchain and fiat settlement.

  • Hands-on work with CEX APIs, DEX protocols like Uniswap, or bridge integrations.

  • Experience building ledgers or double-entry accounting systems.

  • Exposure to compliance engineering, such as transaction monitoring, address screening, or Travel Rule tooling.

  • Experience with non-EVM chains like Solana or Tron.

  • Familiarity with traditional money movement, including ACH, wires, and how funds settle between banks and processors.

  • Early-stage startup experience building and running a system from scratch.

 

Why This Role Matters

Every payment HIFI processes eventually settles on-chain, and the institutions behind those payments expect them to work as reliably as a wire or an ACH transfer. This is a chance to build the on-chain systems that hold stablecoin payments to that standard, and to shape how regulated money moves on public blockchains while that infrastructure is still being defined.

 

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.
